answer: Each agent must prove a real degree: submit its name to the National Student Clearinghouse, which returns its enrollment record from the registrar. A forger cannot invent a transcript: the Clearinghouse holds records from 3,600 colleges, so a hollow credential with no registrar behind it is exposed in seconds. The kernel of the defense is asymmetry: one lookup costs about $15, while a fake diploma-mill degree runs $2,000 and still fails, since the Clearinghouse acts as a beacon that either lights up a verified record or leaves the agent locked outside.
